title: Cheese Pizza, School Lunch, Thick Crust

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese pizza is a popular school lunch option, made on a thick, crunchy crust. The dough typically contains wheat flour, yeast, water and salt, topped with tomato sauce and shredded cheese that melts into a golden layer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A thick crust makes the pizza more filling and holds more sauce.
The cheese used in school pizzas is often a blend of mozzarella and cheddar for better melt and flavor.
Tomato sauce in school pizzas is usually made from tomato paste, salt and a modest amount of spices.
Pizza is included in school nutrition programs in many countries as a source of carbs and calcium.
Traditionally the pizza is cut into 6–8 triangular slices, which are easy for children to handle.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese topping provides calcium, essential for growing bones and teeth in children.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Cheese and any added meat supply animal protein that supports growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The crust delivers complex carbohydrates that give sustained energy for the school day.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomatoes and yeast in the dough contain B1, B2 and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene
items.content: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may help protect cells.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in children with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese often contain added salt, so intake should be moderate, especially for children with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The thick crust and cheese make the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended to avoid over‑eating.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat flour dough contains gluten, which can be problematic for children with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pizza is usually served hot, cut into triangular slices. It can be topped with fresh vegetables or herbs for added nutrition. Children may eat it with their hands or use a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover pizza in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
